items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: lots of the road bands would come through, the Gene Coy and Merle Carlson. ... That was a white band. ... And they had some good players.

ctx.x: That's the Gil Evans we know?

Yeah. After we came back from Tahoe we tried to get a job in Sacramento and we hung around there for a couple weeks. The union wouldn't let us work the club and when you go without food for four or five days it gets a little rough. And we'd all try to think of girls we knew in Sacramento and get invited over to dinner or something and say, well, how about bringing my friends.

So that didn't work out. So we went back to Stockton. We worked in a place called the Dreamland Ballroom and I went back to junior college in Modesto and I used to hitchhike up to Stockton every night and play all night and then hitchhike back in the morning and go to school. And while we were there, lots of the road bands would come through, the Gene Coy and Merle Carlson. Do you remember that band?
